newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares gain 2.09 percent on selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares gain 2.09 percent on selective trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted selective gains in firmer volume on Wednesday in reaction to Tuesday's profit-taking and amid persisting political optimism, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 ended at a day's high 1,951, up 40 points, or 2.09 percent from Tuesday when it fell 2.15 percent. Trade volume rose to 27.18 trillion lira, up 16.7 percent from Tuesday's 23.29 trillion.
Brokers said the market tested the index's resistance at 1,950 after Tuesday's profit taking sales.

"Today's rise was a correction of yesterday's profit-taking. It was helped by the resignation of a deputy from the conservative opposition True Path Party," said Birten Yalcinkaya from Istanbul Securities.
Brokers said activity enlivened in state owned shares which have major impact on the market index due to their high market capitalisation.

"The market got a lift from the opening with selective buying in state owned shares, led by oil refiner Tupras. The banking sector also regained all of its Tuesday losses," said Murat Arslanoglu from Bank Kapital.
The top active stock was Tupras, up 8,000 lira at 98,000, making up 9.4 percent of the overall volume.
Brokers said the main reason boosting activity in Tupras was was its forthcoming capital increase of 2.7 bonuses and 2.7 rights for one existing share, due to start on July 14.

Tupras was followed by Sabanci Holding a leading conglomerate, down 300 lira at 5,900, automotive firm Otosan, up 5,000 lira at 86,000 and largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 500 lira at 24,500. The four most active shares made up 24.6 percent of market volume.
The new right-left coalition headed by conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz will face a confidence vote in parliament on Saturday. The market widely expects the coalition to win the vote.

Of the 247 shares traded, rises outdid the falls sharply by 140 to 49 while 58 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial gained 1.96 percent to 1,824, the IMKB Services inched up 0.58 percent to 1,902 and the IMKB Financial leapt 2.34 percent to 2,143.
The banking sector was the leading gainer with a 3.47 percent premium.
